extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, State Exchanges/SBE-FPs, State regulators, and other health policy stakeholders (issuers, plan management staff, consumer advocates)
extracted.subtask_short: deferring network adequacy reviews to states
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and implementation guidance for (1) discontinuing non-standardized plan option limits and related policies, and (2) deferring network adequacy/provider access reviews from HHS to FFE States that demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity under an Effective Provider Access Review Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted average number of total plans available per enrollee
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary metric used to evaluate plan proliferation: the weighted average number of total QHPs available per enrollee in the FFEs and SBE-FPs (reported for PYs 2020–2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge whether policies (standardized plan options, non-standardized plan option limits/exceptions) meaningfully reduced plan proliferation; noted to have remained relatively constant from PY 2023 to PY 2025 despite added requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted average number of total plans offered per issuer
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric: the weighted average number of total plans offered per issuer (reported for PYs 2020–2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside plans-per-enrollee to evaluate issuer-level effects of policy changes (showed modest decreases after limits were introduced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of enrollment and active selections in non-standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of consumer choice/behavior: percent of enrollees and percent of active plan selections that are non-standardized plan options (examples: 80% enrolment in PY 2023, 67% in PY 2024 and 2025; active selections 82% in PY 2023, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as evidence of consumer preference for non-standardized plans and an indicator of whether standardized plan options meaningfully shift consumer choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of total plan offerings that are non-standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of plan offerings that are non-standardized (e.g., 75% in PY 2023, 72% in PY 2024, 69% in PY 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare expected vs actual enrollment/active selection rates and assess whether non-standardized offerings attract relatively higher uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan-county discontinuation rates and enrollees affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics of market disruption: percent of plan-county combinations discontinued year-to-year and percent of enrollees affected (baseline PY 2020–2022 rates and increases after policy implementation in PY 2023–2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess market disruption attributable to imposing standardized plan options and non-standardized plan option limits; compared against baseline discontinuation rates to infer policy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: AV de minimis range compliance (actuarial value ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that plans meet actuarial value (AV) de minimis ranges per §§156.140, 156.200, and 156.400; narrowing of ranges (e.g., on-Exchange silver from 66–72% to 70–72%) forced discontinuation or modification of some plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledged as contributing to discontinuations but not fully explaining elevated discontinuation rates after other policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer decision complexity and plan comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: reduce decision complexity by enhancing plan comparability (theory that standardized cost sharing parameters enable consumers to focus on premiums, networks, formularies, quality ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criterion: whether standardization actually simplifies selection in practice — HHS finds standardization for a subset of plans may add another variable and not materially reduce complexity because consumers rely on premiums, networks, and issuer brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer burden and regulatory complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of producer-side burden: administrative burden and fixed costs for issuers associated with creating/submitting additional certification applications and HHS reviewing and certifying additional plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a negative consequence of standardized plan requirements and non-standardized plan option limits; used to weigh net benefits of policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on issuer innovation and consumer choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion whether policies constrain issuers' ability to innovate plan design (e.g., tiered networks, separate medical/drug deductibles/MOOPs, HSA-eligible HDHPs, >4 drug tiers) and thereby reduce consumer choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify discontinuation of non-standardized plan option limits when disadvantages (inhibited innovation, constrained choice) outweigh marginal reductions in plan proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network adequacy: sufficiency in number and types of providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline Federal standard (Exchange Establishment Rule §156.230): an issuer of a QHP that uses a provider network must maintain a network sufficient in number and types of providers, including providers specializing in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure services are accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in HHS-conducted reviews and as a core standard States must be consistent with to be considered to have sufficient authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and distance standards for network adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative time and distance standards established at §156.230(a)(2) (and in issuer guidance) to assess whether plans meet time/distance requirements for provider access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by HHS in FFE reviews beginning PY 2023 and by States expected to meet Federal-equivalent standards unless deferral criteria apply; States may also propose alternative, administrable standards sensitive to local conditions under proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment wait time standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment wait time standards adopted to start in PY 2025 and required in FFE issuers' processes: enrollees should be able to schedule an appointment at least 90% of the time within 15 business days for routine primary care, within 10 business days for behavioral health providers, and within 30 business days for routine specialty providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS uses issuer-submitted provider lists and secret shopper surveys to measure compliance; applied in QHP certification and enforcement contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Essential Community Providers (ECPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a QHP issuer that uses a network ensure its network, as available to all enrollees, includes ECPs in accordance with §156.235.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the criteria an FFE State must ensure as part of an Effective Provider Access Review Program (see proposed §155.1050(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS data collection, network adequacy templates, and geocoding analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational requirement: FFE issuers must submit a Network Adequacy (NA) template with in-network provider/facility information (NPI, specialty, addresses) that HHS uses for geocoding analyses and to build Provider Population Files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS continues collecting standardized data to support Federal reviews, provide continuity for States, and make standardized data available to States determined to have Effective Provider Access Review Programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret shopper appointment wait time surveys administered by third-party entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning Jan 1, 2025, FFE QHP issuers must contract with a third-party entity to administer secret shopper surveys on a sample of in-network providers to determine compliance with appointment wait time standards for specified provider types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS uses submitted network templates to generate samples and the Appointment Wait Time Secret Shopper Survey Technical Guidance to implement; this is part of QA for appointment wait time compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use and limits of accreditation as proxy for network adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Past policy used issuer accreditation (NCQA, URAC, AAAHC) as a basis for determining network adequacy where States lacked review capacity, but commenters and courts raised concerns about accreditation standards being non-public and accreditors lacking regulatory authority or complaint monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informational criterion cautioning reliance on accreditation alone; influences design of deferral and State-capacity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for alternative, State-specific network adequacy approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that one-size-fits-all Federal approaches may be unsuitable; States may assess access by service availability, time or distance individually, provider-enrollee ratios, adjust standards for remote/urban areas, expand/change provider types, and implement other innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal to empower FFE States that demonstrate capacity to innovate and tailor network adequacy reviews sensitive to local demographics, topography, and market conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan access standard (payment-in-full acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that a QHP issuer that does not use a network (a non-network plan) provide access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and behavioral health providers, to ensure services are accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to States with Effective Provider Access Review Programs per proposed §155.1050(d)(3) and is distinct from standards for network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (1): statutory/regulatory provider access standards and delegation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has established provider access standards in State statute or regulation consistent with §156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii), and reports to HHS whether the State has delegated authority to some entity other than the State Department of Insurance to perform any or all provider access review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First of the proposed six required elements for a State to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program under proposed §155.1050(d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (2): reporting systems and documentation of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process includes reporting systems for State-required provider access metrics and documentation of methodology; the State provides descriptions of data collection systems, resources, templates, and methodologies used by the State or delegated entity, and the State receives from issuers data and documentation sufficient to conduct the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures State technical capacity and transparency in data collection and analytic methods for network adequacy reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (3): compliance procedures and enforcement frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process includes procedures to ensure full and ongoing compliance with State provider access standards and enforcement frameworks so that issuers that fail to meet standards come into compliance, including standardized processes to assess issuer remediation efforts and any justification and exception processes for issuers unable to meet requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates State capacity to enforce standards and manage exceptions and remediation consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (4): regular review procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State establishes and maintains clear procedures and timeline requirements for regular provider access reviews, including processes that ensure reviews occur prior to each plan year's QHP certification cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reviews are timely and aligned with QHP certification cycles to prevent gaps in consumer protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (5): consumer complaint monitoring and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related provider access complaints to ensure sufficient access to providers consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(B) of the ACA and as set forth in State statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects the importance of complaint-driven surveillance and responsiveness as part of a State's review program.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criterion (6): non-network plan data collection and review
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process to collect and review information sufficient to show that non-network plans provide access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies State responsibility to assess non-network plan adequacy using appropriate evidence and documentation.
